mechanism_narrative: An increase in GDP indicates strong economic activity, which should positively impact S&P 500 returns over the next 60 days.
failure_condition: If GDP growth is positive but S&P 500 returns are negative over the next 60 days.

mechanism_narrative: A rise in unemployment rate above 5% signals economic weakness, leading to negative S&P 500 returns in the next 20 days.
failure_condition: If unemployment exceeds 5% but S&P 500 returns are positive.

mechanism_narrative: If unemployment rises while employment does not grow, it indicates economic stagnation, leading to negative S&P 500 returns in 20 days.
failure_condition: If the trigger conditions are met but returns are positive.

mechanism_narrative: A rise in federal funds rate above 4.5% indicates tightening, leading to negative S&P 500 returns in 20 days.
failure_condition: If FEDFUNDS exceeds 4.5% but returns are positive.

mechanism_narrative: High inflation leads to negative S&P 500 returns over 60 days.
failure_condition: If inflation is high but returns are positive.

mechanism_narrative: A decline in industrial production below 110 indicates supply issues, leading to negative S&P 500 returns in 60 days.
failure_condition: If production is below 110 but returns are positive.

mechanism_narrative: If GDP growth slows but housing starts rise, it may indicate a positive economic shift, leading to S&P 500 gains in 20 days.
failure_condition: If the trigger conditions are met but returns are negative.

mechanism_narrative: High retail sales in a late-cycle expansion may not prevent market decline, leading to negative S&P 500 returns in 20 days.
failure_condition: If retail sales are high in late-cycle but returns are positive.
